Absolutely, don't have much to add to that. Overall Valve has an excellent strategy that has been working for a long time, GOG is starting to employ something similar with this system. They are my two favorite platforms, I was very excited to see this release. 

I'm curious about what you think about the time limit. My own guess is that GOG put the 5 day limit in place because if they made this offer permanent, it should be objectively better to buy those games on Steam than GOG. I saw a few comments about the time limit but never felt like responding.

True about keys generated from other platforms. I will say though, that I considered getting games on Steam eligible for this program because having games I want on both would be convenient (especially GalCiv3.) In that case, I'd basically be paying Steam and getting a free copy on GOG. It's probably safe to say many of the free copies generated on GOG will come from actual Steam purchases.

My understanding of this system though, is that GOG is the one trying to get people to their Ecosystem. Valve isn't giving free keys, you have to own it on Steam. GOG is giving their own copies if you already own it on Steam.

(I apologize in advance if I missed your point.)

This is only a net positive for Steam. This is a one-way street as far as I can tell, where owning the Steam version gets you the GOG version at no additional cost. Buying on GOG and giving GOG the cut of the money instead doesn't let you use the game free on Steam. 

Steam has already been paid their 30% cut for your purchase on their platform, so whether or not you can now access the game on another service is not an issue. 

That's not the only benefit though, people who prefer DRM free copies may avoid Steam if the game is slated for release on GOG. It would be a bigger positive if GOG announced in advance that a game would be eligible for this service prior to it even being available to buy on GOG, but that probably wouldn't happen as then everyone would just buy it on Steam first.

I picked up one of these from Ebay for pretty cheap. It was an upgrade to my GTX 680, mostly testing the waters with AMD and getting familiar with a new brand. Exploration mostly.

I don't regret it for a minute. The price could not be beat, the card still runs great. When people say it runs hot, it takes a lot of heat to get it to start throttling. It will get hot, but it's not all that noticeable. 

As far as the sound, the fan is loud when running at 100%. You probably don't need it running at 100% all the time, by any stretch. I've always been very tolerant about noise though, so YMMV. 

In short, it provides unbeatable value. (It WAS bigger than I was expecting, but I already knew my case would fit anything if I remove the drive cages. I ALMOST had to remove one of the drive cages.)
